niche: a media group's web platform team choosing which of six properties gets its one performance squad for a quarter, by the page loads a month the squad's hero-image playbook would move into the good Largest Contentful Paint band, from RUM beacons that break each load's paint into its four parts
answer: Trailhead: its hero-image playbook would move 4.9 million page loads a month into the good LCP band, 1.44 times Pantry's 3.3 million
stakeholder_role: the group's head of web platform

spine.entity: one row is one sampled page load's RUM beacon with its Largest Contentful Paint attribution (element, resource URL and the four parts of the paint)

world.org_type: digital media group with six properties

driver: The decisive quantity is how many units an intervention moves across a threshold when its effect, measured on past applications, works through a step that needs a reference each unit's own served document must carry; every past application ran on units whose documents carried it, so the back-test passes by construction, while part of the forward population assembles its document after delivery and the step cannot reach it, which only a crawl of the served documents joined unit by unit shows; the candidate the validated effect favours most loses most of its gain and one no wrong construction ranks first leads
driver_concrete: Each property's November page loads whose LCP element is its own hero image are rebuilt part by part as the squad's engagements show the playbook lands (the image's load delay at the CDN connection level, load time at the AVIF ratio, each paint floored at the load's own first contentful paint), but the preload that brings the delay to that level is written into the page's server-rendered head and can only name a hero the page's HTML carries: on Matchday's live pages, Tideline's live pages, Ledger's markets pages and Pantry's planner pages the 2 December crawl shows a shell whose only image is the logo, the app putting the hero in after its script runs, so those loads keep their delay and none moves; every engaged site served its hero in the article HTML. Matchday falls from 6.3 to 3.4 million and Trailhead leads at 4.9 million.
stump: A competent analyst rebuilds each slow own-image page load the way the squad's engagements show the playbook lands, the image's load delay at the 240 ms the engagements settled at, its load time at their ratio and each paint no sooner than the load's own first contentful paint, and files Matchday, 6.3 million page loads a month; the preload that brings the delay to that level sits in the page's server HTML and can only name a hero that HTML carries, and on Matchday's live pages and the other app sections the crawl shows a shell with no hero, so those loads keep their delay, Matchday moves 3.4 million and Trailhead leads at 4.9 million.
analyst_test: A strong analyst who weights the November beacons to page loads, keeps the slow loads whose paint element is the property's own hero image, rebuilds each one's paint part by part with the engagements' delay level and load time ratio and floors it at the load's own first contentful paint (the construction both portal responses reached) files Matchday (6.3 million page loads a month); ratios of medians or the preload rule of thumb file Ledger (8.8 and 9.7 million); the level with the render delay held files Pantry (8.1 million); only the level and the floor applied where the page's server HTML carries the hero, every other load keeping its own delay, files Trailhead (4.9 million).
domain_test: The call turns on how many page loads a month cross under the 2,500 ms Largest Contentful Paint line when a hero-image playbook changes two of the paint's four parts, estimated as web performance engineers do from RUM attribution and the playbook's measured effect, with what the change cannot reach kept as it is: a preload from the document head can only fetch an image the server HTML names, and the paint can never come before the page's first paint; with a hospital's or a utility's nouns there is no paint split into parts, no preload scanner, no server-rendered document against a client-rendered one and no first paint, and the task stops reading the same.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many units an intervention moves across a threshold when it acts on two of the four additive parts of each unit's value, and the record of past interventions shows one of those parts settling at a fixed level rather than shrinking in proportion, rising where it began below that level, so the units it can move are those whose untouched parts leave room under the threshold once that part sits at its level, built unit by unit; carrying the past effect as a ratio of medians, or as one cut to the whole value, picks a candidate whose small starting part the ratio shrinks further.

lineage.driver: The decisive quantity is how many units an intervention moves across a threshold when it acts on two of the four additive parts of each unit's value: the record of past interventions shows one part settling at a fixed level rather than shrinking in proportion, and each unit's value never falling below a second measure of the same unit that the intervention leaves alone, which on a share of units sits beyond the threshold; built unit by unit with the level and that floor, the candidate the level favours most loses most of its gain to the floor and a third leads, while a ratio of the past effect picks a candidate whose small starting part it shrinks further and the level without the floor picks the floored candidate.
lineage.stump: A competent analyst carries the squad's past engagements onto each slow own-image page load as ratios, the image's load delay and load time each cut by the after-over-before ratio of medians and the rest of the paint held, and files Ledger, 7.4 million page loads a month into the good band; the delay settles at one level instead (240 ms, the CDN connection), which puts Pantry first at 6.8 million with the render delay held, and the paint cannot come before the page's own first contentful paint, which the playbook leaves where it is: most of Pantry's slow loads sit on pages that first paint about three seconds after their first byte, so it moves 2.9 million and Matchday leads at 4.6 million.

notes: drawn 2026-10-13 ahead of task257 (DA07), whose world turns on the duty-cycle mix (composition_mix), barred by ban.strategy against task256; the seed's own decisive hint (fixes only moved loads whose paint element was the property's own image) is kept as a lower rung (the reachable population), never decisive; the decisive move is the shape of the playbook's effect on the image's load delay Stage 3 (2026-10-13): built; the sampling rates were evened so that no wrong rung lands on Pantry without weights, Trailhead resized so Pantry sits 5th on rung 0, the engagements' samples tightened so every estimator of the level and ratio gives the same rounded counts.
